chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Sufi narrated to us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Aqil narrated from Ishaq ibn Rahwayh, saying:

When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Naysabur and intended to depart from there to al-Ma'mun, the traditionists gathered around him and said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! You are leaving us without narrating a hadith to us so that we may derive benefit from it?

He was sitting in the 'ammariyyah (a camel-borne sedan), so he leaned his head out and said: I heard my father Musa ibn Ja'far say: I heard my father Ja'far ibn Muhammad say: I heard my father Muhammad ibn 'Ali say: I heard my father 'Ali ibn al-Husayn say: I heard my father al-Husayn ibn 'Ali ibn Abi Talib say: I heard my father the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali ibn Abi Talib say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say: I heard Jibra'il say: I heard Allah, Exalted be His Glory, say: 'There is no god but Allah is My Fortress. Whoever enters it is safe from My chastisement.'
He said: Then when the camel passed by, he called out to us: 'It is subject to conditions, and I am among its conditions.'

The Compiler of this book explains: Among its conditions is the acknowledgment that al-Rida (peace be upon him) is an Imam appointed by Allah, the Mighty and High, over the servants, with obedience to him being obligatory upon them.

key_terms.الْعَمَّارِيَّةُ: A camel-borne sedan or litter used for travel
key_terms.حِصْنِي: My Fortress, referring to the declaration of monotheism
key_terms.شُرُوطِهَا: Its conditions, referring to the prerequisites for the promise of safety

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Imam al-Rida being described as a condition for entering Allah's Fortress?
ai.summary: In this renowned hadith from al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the theological link between monotheism (*Tawhid*) and Imamate by presenting a continuous chain of transmission from Allah to Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and down through the Imams. He declares 'La ilaha illallah' as Allah’s fortress for safety from chastisement, and upon his departure, clarifies that he himself is among the 'conditions' for entering this fortress, signifying that recognizing his divinely appointed Imamate is essential for the validity of one's faith and salvation.
